"2.

In the said judgment, the Court held as under :-
"22.
sentences._hearing_file: Dipakbhai Juvansing Brahmbhatt vs State Of Gujarat & on 22 September, 2017.json

sentences.text: It is only retroactive criminal legislation that is prohibited under Article 20(1).
sentences._hearing_file: Dipakbhai Juvansing Brahmbhatt vs State Of Gujarat & on 22 September, 2017.json

sentences.text: The prohibition contained in Article 20(1) is that no person shall be convicted of any offence except for violation of a law in force at the time of the commission of the act charged as an offence prohibits nor shall he be subjected to a penalty greater than that which might have been inflicted under the law in force at the time of the commission of the offence.
sentences._hearing_file: Dipakbhai Juvansing Brahmbhatt vs State Of Gujarat & on 22 September, 2017.json

sentences.text: It is quite clear HC-NIC Page 4 of 6 Created On Mon Oct 02 03:32:20 IST 2017 R/CR.RA/573/2016 JUDGMENT that insofar as the Central Amendment Act creates new offences or enhances punishment for a particular type of offence no person can be convicted by such ex post facto law nor can the enhanced punishment prescribed by the amendment be applicable.
sentences._hearing_file: Dipakbhai Juvansing Brahmbhatt vs State Of Gujarat & on 22 September, 2017.json

sentences.text: But insofar as the Central Amendment Act reduces the punishment for an offence punishable under Section 16(1)(a) of the Act, there is no reason why the accused should not have the benefit of such reduced punishment.
sentences._hearing_file: Dipakbhai Juvansing Brahmbhatt vs State Of Gujarat & on 22 September, 2017.json

sentences.text: The rule of beneficial construction requires that even ex post facto law of such a type should be applied to mitigate the rigour of the law.
sentences._hearing_file: Dipakbhai Juvansing Brahmbhatt vs State Of Gujarat & on 22 September, 2017.json

sentences.text: The principle is based both on sound reason and common sense.
sentences._hearing_file: Dipakbhai Juvansing Brahmbhatt vs State Of Gujarat & on 22 September, 2017.json

sentences.text: A retrospective statute is different from an ex post facto statute.
sentences._hearing_file: Dipakbhai Juvansing Brahmbhatt vs State Of Gujarat & on 22 September, 2017.json

sentences.text:
"Every ex post facto law...."
said Chase, J., in the American case of Calder v. Bull "must necessarily be retrospective, but every retrospective law is not an ex post facto law.
sentences._hearing_file: Dipakbhai Juvansing Brahmbhatt vs State Of Gujarat & on 22 September, 2017.json

sentences.text: Every law that takes away or impairs rights vested agreeably to existing laws is retrospective, and is generally unjust and may be oppressive; it is a good general rule that a law should have no retrospect, but in cases in which the laws may justly and for the benefit of the community and also of individuals relate to a time antecedent to their commencement: as statutes of oblivion or of pardon.
sentences._hearing_file: Dipakbhai Juvansing Brahmbhatt vs State Of Gujarat & on 22 September, 2017.json

sentences.text: They are certainly retrospective, and literally both concerning and after the facts committed.
sentences._hearing_file: Dipakbhai Juvansing Brahmbhatt vs State Of Gujarat & on 22 September, 2017.json

sentences.text: But I do not consider any law ex post facto within the prohibition that mollifies the rigour of the criminal law, but only those that create or aggravate the crime, or increase the punishment or change the rules of evidence for HC-NIC Page 5 of 6 Created On Mon Oct 02 03:32:20 IST 2017 R/CR.RA/573/2016 JUDGMENT the purpose of conviction....
sentences._hearing_file: Dipakbhai Juvansing Brahmbhatt vs State Of Gujarat & on 22 September, 2017.json

sentences.text: There is a great and apparent difference between making an unlawful act lawful and the making an innocent action criminal and punishing it as a crime."
sentences._hearing_file: Dipakbhai Juvansing Brahmbhatt vs State Of Gujarat & on 22 September, 2017.json

sentences.text: From the facts of the present case, we have no doubt in mind that the aforesaid judgment squarely applies thereon.

A retrospective statute is different from an ex post facto statute.
From the facts of the present case, we have no doubt in mind that the aforesaid judgment squarely applies thereon.
